entries.message: expected a component element and received {received}.
entries.fix: Pass the element whose loop is intentional — `allowRenderLoop(this)` inside the component.

entries.message: returned a promise — an async callback runs, but it cannot return a cleanup, and what it awaits may arrive after the component re-ran or was removed.
entries.fix: To cancel it, write the effect as a plain function that starts the async work and returns a cleanup that stops it — for a fetch, `const c = new AbortController(); load(c.signal); return () => c.abort();`.

entries.message: init() was given a built-in element (a div, a section…), which has no lifecycle core can hear: it is never set up again when re-attached and never released when removed.
entries.fix: Use a custom element and call init(this) in its connectedCallback — or, to keep the built-in element, wire its lifecycle: wire([renderer, nativeElements]) from '@verajs/renderer/native-elements'.

entries.message: expected a function and received {received}: the hook's callback runs on every change it follows.
entries.fix: Pass the function itself (`effect(() => …)`), not its result (`effect(fn())`), and check a callback read from options is defined.

entries.message: threw (the function a hook returned, not the hook itself); its error is printed beside this line, and the rest of the teardown ran.
entries.fix: Fix the cleanup, or wire an 'error' insert to handle what hooks throw.

entries.message: read its own value while computing it, directly or through another computed, so it has no value to give.
entries.fix: A computed cannot depend on itself: keep the previous value in a signal you write, and read that instead.

entries.message: expected a function to derive the value from, and received {received}.
entries.fix: Pass the expression as a function — computed(() => a + b), not computed(a + b).

entries.message: was given deep: {received}, which is not true or false, so it used its default.
entries.fix: Pass a boolean: signal(value, { deep: true }).

entries.message: `foreignNodes: {value}` is not a setting, so the template owns this root (the default, 'drop').
entries.fix: Use 'drop' (the template owns the root: foreign nodes are cleared when the template changes) or 'preserve' (the root keeps them where they are).

entries.message: threw; its error is printed beside this line, and the other hooks still ran.
entries.fix: Fix the hook, or wire an 'error' insert to handle what hooks throw: `wire([{ on: 'error', fn: (error, element) => … }])`.

entries.message: expected a component element and received {received}.
entries.fix: Call it in connectedCallback with the component itself — `init(this)`.

entries.message: `init`'s second argument is the SETUP, a function, and this is an options object (the old `init(this, { mode })`): it is ignored, in every build, so this component sets up with no shadow root.
entries.fix: Options travel with the host: `init({ host: this, shadow: 'open' }, setup)`.

entries.message: called init() twice in one setup, so the {hooks} hook(s) registered since the first call were discarded and will never run.
entries.fix: init() starts a fresh generation of hooks — which is what makes it safe when a component reconnects — so anything registered before a second call is dropped. Call init() once, then register hooks, then render() or mount().

entries.message: is an automatic list, but the full renderer is not wired, so the list cannot commit its own rows: every row's change re-renders the whole parent instead.
entries.fix: Wire them together once at your entry — wire([renderer, lists]) — rather than lists beside a bare { on: 'render', fn: renderInto }.

entries.message: returned templates, but no list module is wired, so its rows are matched by position: reorder the array and a row's DOM state (a focused input, a typed value) and its component state show against another item.
entries.fix: Wire the automatic lists once at your entry — wire([renderer, lists]) with lists from @verajs/renderer/keyed — or key each row with keyed(key, row). To match by position on purpose (rows with no state), map a plain copy: [...state.rows].map(…).

entries.message: flush() inside a running flush (a hook, a render, or an event one of them fired) does nothing: the DOM updates when this flush ends — nothing failed.
entries.fix: To read the DOM a render made, read it in an effect with `{ timing: 'layout' }`, which runs right after the render.

entries.message: works, but nothing that reads it updates when it changes.
entries.fix: Make it reactive: `import { collections } from '@verajs/store/collections'` and add it to your `wire([…])` call.

entries.message: there is no component being set up. Hooks belong to a component's setup — the function `init` calls, synchronously — so after it returns, after an `await` inside it, or later in a handler, there is no component to attach them to.
entries.fix: Called after an `await` in an async setup? Call effect() BEFORE the first `await`, and return the render after it. To change what is shown later, write to a store. A builder's own primitive names its owner: `effect(fn, { owner })`.

entries.message: no renderer is wired, so nothing will appear.
entries.fix: Wire one once, at your app entry: `import { renderer } from '@verajs/renderer'; wire([renderer]);`

entries.message: `{key}` is claimed by {first} and by {second}, so both are handed it and either may read it.
entries.fix: Wire only one module that takes this option, or ask the module to rename its key.

entries.message: was given persist: {received}, which is not a finite number of seconds, so it is torn down at removal.
entries.fix: Pass the seconds to keep it paused after a removal — init({ host: this, persist: 30 }) — or leave persist out.

entries.message: the priority must be a finite number, and {received} is not — the hook was not registered (in production too, silently).
entries.fix: Lower runs first: 25 runs before the render, 50 is the render, 60 a layout effect, 75 an effect. A priority read from config with `parseInt` is NaN when the value is missing.

entries.message: read an object from `{key}`, a property locked with defineProperty (non-writable, non-configurable), which a store must hand back exactly as it is: it is not a store, so changes inside it render nothing.
entries.fix: Do not lock the slot with defineProperty; to read an object as it is on purpose, freeze the parent object.

entries.message: has re-run for {frames} consecutive frames because it writes state it also reads — this will keep running for as long as the page is open.
entries.fix: Guard the write (`if (next !== state.x) state.x = next`), or move it out of the pass. More than one hook may be involved: a template reading what an effect writes is caught here too. If it is deliberate — an animation driven by one store write per frame — silence it with `allowRenderLoop(this)` from @verajs/core, or drive it with `requestAnimationFrame`.

entries.message: wrote `{key}` the value it already has, on a key the language would refuse to write (read-only, or a frozen object): nothing changed, so nothing is thrown, but a write that CHANGES it throws.
entries.fix: To check first: `Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor(obj, key)?.writable`, or `Object.isFrozen(snapshot(obj))`.

entries.message: expected a function and received {received}.
entries.fix: It receives the flush and decides when to run it — `microtask` (the default) and `frameBudget` are exported for that.

entries.message: it has a `{name}` method and no `setup`, so init found nothing to run.
entries.fix: Name the method `setup` — init(this) calls `this.setup(host)` and renders the function it returns.

entries.message: was removed while its async setup was still running, and the setup had not settled {seconds} s later — so it was torn down without ever drawing.
entries.fix: If the component may come back later, let the setup finish faster (pass its abort signal to fetch), or keep it with persist: seconds.

entries.message: its async setup rejected, so nothing it registered runs; the error is printed beside this line.
entries.fix: Catch inside the setup to render a fallback, or wire an 'error' insert to handle it: `wire([{ on: 'error', fn: (error, element) => … }])`.

entries.message: `shadow: {value}` names a mode the platform does not have, so attachShadow refuses it (it throws, in every build).
entries.fix: Use 'open', 'closed', false (light DOM) or a ShadowRootInit such as { mode: 'open', delegatesFocus: true }.

entries.message: core's own store handlers were handed to the store door twice, which means two copies of core's traps module were bundled into one copy of core.
entries.fix: This is a build error: check that the bundler resolves core to one module graph.

entries.message: expected an object and received {received}.
entries.fix: To hold one value, use signal(value).

entries.message: this store's source object refused the {operation} — {why}.
entries.fix: A store proxies the object it was given and cannot override what JavaScript declines. Pass a mutable object to createStore, or keep this one outside the store and read it directly.

entries.message: {cls} defines its own `{name}`, which runs with the raw array as `this`: a field it writes is not tracked (the items and the length are).
entries.fix: Keep that state in the store beside the list (`state.list.push(x); state.added++`), derive it (`computed(() => state.list.length)`), or write the field through the store.

entries.message: re-entered 50 times and was stopped — it writes state it also reads, and it runs synchronously on every change, so an unguarded write feeds itself.
entries.fix: Guard the write (`if (next !== state.x) state.x = next`), or use a plain `effect`, which coalesces.

entries.message: expected a function and received {received}.
entries.fix: It runs the function without subscribing — `untrack(() => state.a)`, not `untrack(state.a)`, which reads the property before untrack can do anything about it.

entries.message: renders `{attribute}`, but no directives engine is wired, so that attribute does nothing.
entries.fix: `@verajs/directives` is NOT PUBLISHED YET — `npm i` will 404 — so if this markup came from a demo, remove the attribute or write the behavior yourself for now. When it ships, it is wired once at your app entry: `import { directives } from '@verajs/directives'; wire([renderer, directives]);`

entries.message: declares `static styles`, but nothing is adopting them, so it renders unstyled.
entries.fix: Style adoption lives in `@verajs/styles`. Wire it once at your app entry: `import { styles } from '@verajs/styles'; wire([styles]);`

entries.message: was handed back as it is before the module that makes it reactive was wired, and stays that way: wiring later reaches only values not read yet.
entries.fix: Wire store modules before creating stores (`wire([collections])` first, in the entry).
